newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Karachi bourse seeks tax exemptions in June budget.
newsitem.headline: Karachi bourse seeks tax exemptions in June budget.

text.p: Pakistan's main Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) said on Wednesday it had asked Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government for exemption from various taxes to help boost portfolio investment in a cash-strapped stock market.
The demands have been sent to the Finance Ministry for incorporation in the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July/June), a KSE statement said. The demands are:
- Extension of exemption available on capital gains up to June 1998 for five more years.
- Removal of anolmalies regarding tax exemption for bonus shares issued to shareholders.
- Tax exemption on investment made by investors in mutual funds or in the capital markets through mutual funds.
- Extension to all entities trading in shares of the exemption from turnover tax now available to state-run National Investment Trust and the Investment Corporation of Pakistan.

- Removal of anomalies regarding exemption of tax on capital gains for insurance companies and the extension of this exemption, which ends in June 1998, to June 1999 to allow insurance companies to act as major investors in the market.
- Early introduction of a legal framework allowing the 782 listed companies to buy back their own shares.
